name: Tu Ch’iu-niang
bio: Tu Ch’iu-niang is dated by Giles to the 8th or 9th century AD. Her poem here urges the young not to waste their hours of youth.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Golden Sands
poems.author: Tu Ch’iu-niang
poems.text:
I would not have thee grudge those robes which gleam in rich array,
But I would have thee grudge the hours of youth which glide away.
Go pluck the blooming flower betimes, lest when thou com'st again
Alas, upon the withered stem no blooming flowers remain!

poems.title: The Gold-Threaded Robe
poems.author: Tu Ch’iu-niang
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
Covet not a gold-threaded robe,
Cherish only your young days!
If a bud open, gather it —
Lest you but wait for an empty bough.
